title: The dryer at the launderette kept my name 🧺
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 1:12 in the morning the dryer at the launderette finished a load I never put in.

scenes.narration: At 1:12 in the morning the dryer at the launderette finished a load I never put in.
I was the only customer. The place smells of hot lint and cheap soap, and the clock above the door has been broken for a year.
Machine seven stopped. The door clicked open by itself. Inside, a warm, tidy pile of clothes, folded as if somebody had been very careful.
I picked up the top one. A grey jumper. My jumper, the one I lost two years ago, the one with the small hole at the cuff.
There were more. My old school scarf. A coat I buried in the back of a wardrobe at my mum's. Each one still warm, and none of them mine to find here.
A paper tag was pinned to the last one. Collected from every place you have ever been lonely. Please take them all home.
I put them back and walked towards the door. Behind me every machine in the row clicked open at once, and every drum was full.
The shop phone rang. A soft voice said, your wash is ready, it is a very big load. And the next load, it said, is you.
So tell me. Do you take the clothes, or leave without them?
